// Fixture source for the complexity-coverage ratchet — NOT compiled.
//
// It carries `.ts.txt` rather than `.ts` on purpose: a real `.ts` here would be
// swept by this very guard, by the file-size ratchet and by `tsc`, so a fixture
// that must FAIL would fail the live tree it is only supposed to describe.
//
// `routeDispatch` is one exported function with twenty-one branch points — the
// shape an agent lands when nothing counts them: every condition inline, no
// test in the package naming it.

export interface DispatchRequest {
  lane?: string;
  mode?: string;
  retries?: number;
  labels?: string[];
  urgent?: boolean;
  owner?: string | null;
}

export function routeDispatch(request: DispatchRequest, budget: number): string {
  let lane = request.lane ?? "default";
  if (request.mode === "scout") {
    lane = "scout";
  } else if (request.mode === "go") {
    lane = "go";
  } else if (request.mode === "afk" && budget > 0) {
    lane = "afk";
  }

  const retries = request.retries ?? 0;
  for (const label of request.labels ?? []) {
    if (label === "blocked") return "parked";
    if (label === "urgent" || label === "hot") {
      lane = retries > 3 ? "escalated" : "priority";
    }
    switch (label) {
      case "docs":
        lane = "docs";
        break;
      case "release":
        lane = "release";
        break;
      case "chore":
        lane = budget > 10 ? "chore" : lane;
        break;
      default:
        break;
    }
  }

  while (retries > 0 && budget > 0 && lane === "default") {
    lane = "retry";
  }

  try {
    if (request.owner === null) {
      lane = request.urgent ? "unowned-urgent" : "unowned";
    }
  } catch {
    lane = "broken";
  }

  do {
    if (lane === "retry" && budget < 2) lane = "starved";
  } while (false);

  return lane;
}
